title: H0273 (2020 Regular): Carrying of Firearms

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk data (gun-policy Stage 5, Florida); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Florida text (Introduced, 2019-10-01; official copy, https://www.flsenate.gov/Session/Bill/2020/273/BillText/Filed/PDF (LegiScan doc 2055422))
provenance.note: Read as filed (Introduced, 2019-10-01); no vote. Struck: the license requirement in s. 790.01(2), felony of the third degree (now second-degree misdemeanor), the nonresident conditions in s. 790.015, the open-carry firearm ban in s. 790.053, 'other than a handgun' in s. 790.25(5). Sections 4, 6, 8, 9 are conforming (pharmacy possession, school guardian license requirement struck, employee definition, ranking chart entry for carrying a concealed firearm struck); treated as part of the carry change.

operative_text: Section 1 (s. 790.01, F.S.): Except as provided in subsection (3), a person who carries a concealed firearm on or about his or her person into any place described in s. 790.06(12)(a) commits a misdemeanor of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082 or, s. 775.083, Section 2 (s. 790.015, F.S.): All valid licenses to carry concealed weapons and firearms issued by other states are hereby given full faith and credit in this state. Section 5 (s. 790.25, F.S.): A person not otherwise prohibited by law from possessing a firearm. Nothing herein contained prohibits the carrying of a legal firearm anywhere in a private conveyance when such firearm is being carried for a lawful use.
